description: Design a Base64 decoder using ARM's Scalable Vector Extension (SVE/SVE2) that is Vector-Length Agnostic (VLA), automatically scaling from 128-bit to 2048-bit vector widths without code changes. SVE's predication and first-faulting loads enable clean tail handling and error detection.
mathematical_formalization: Let VL = vector length in bytes. Each iteration: p = whilelt(i, n); data = svld1_u8(p, &input[i]); decode VL bytes; store (3/4)*VL bytes. Loop terminates when svptest_any(p) is false. The algorithm is VL-independent.
analogical_connections: GPU SIMT: warp-level programming where lane count is abstracted
implementation_hypothesis: Use svtbl for table lookup, svmad for bit packing, svst1 with predicates for masked stores. Test on Graviton3 (256-bit SVE) and A64FX (512-bit SVE).
experiment_seed: Cross-compile for SVE, benchmark on Graviton3 via AWS. Compare against hand-tuned NEON. Test same binary on 512-bit SVE simulator.
